clue.text: Deliberately ignore one's skin

parts.note: to cut someone is to snub them on purpose
one is I, and 's stands for is

explanation.surface: Someone advised to pay no attention to their own complexion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's' reads as a possessive but is I plus 's, short for is.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutis is the anatomical Latin term for the dermis, the true layer of the body's outer covering.

clue.text: When caught, Arabs pay out for such creatures

parts.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: out here means wrong or disordered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters as written

explanation.surface: Traders who pay up when caught out, for some animals.
explanation.walkthrough: The C for caught joins the fodder before the letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Capybaras are large South American rodents, so they are examples of creatures.

clue.text: Hardy girl grabbing the queen's hair

indicators.note: someone grabbing something holds it inside their grasp, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: Tess of the d'Urbervilles, Thomas Hardy's heroine
R for Regina, the queen

explanation.surface: A tough young woman seizing a lock of the monarch's hair.
explanation.walkthrough: Hardy looks like an adjective meaning tough, but it is the novelist Thomas Hardy.
explanation.definitionFit: A tress is a long lock of a woman's hair.

clue.text: Fish kept in pen — a way to achieve balance

indicators.note: kept in means held inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a pig pen is a sty
an eel is a fish
taken as written
Rd, road, is a way

explanation.surface: A fish held in an enclosure, as a means of keeping things steady.
explanation.walkthrough: Pen suggests writing, but it is an animal enclosure; Rd, road, is the usual crossword way.
explanation.definitionFit: A steelyard is a weighing balance with a sliding counterweight on a long arm.

clue.text: Buffet having difficulty providing illumination

parts.note: to buffet is to hit hard, to lam
a plight is a difficult situation; having signals it is attached

explanation.surface: A sideboard of food in trouble, somehow still lighting up the room.
explanation.walkthrough: Buffet suggests a spread of food, but here it is the verb meaning to strike.
explanation.definitionFit: Lamplight is the glow given off by a lamp, a kind of lighting.

clue.text: Youngster constantly seen in bar

indicators.note: seen in means appearing within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a let is a hindrance, as in 'without let or hindrance'
ever means always, constantly

explanation.surface: A young person who is always to be found in the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: Bar suggests a pub but is LET, an obstacle; the youngster is an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A leveret is a hare in its first year, a young animal.

clue.text: Accountants in a haze, having added up wrongly

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a mist is a haze
CAs are chartered accountants

explanation.surface: Bewildered bookkeepers who have totted up the figures incorrectly.
explanation.walkthrough: To cast a column of figures is an old phrase for adding it up.
explanation.definitionFit: To miscast is to total figures incorrectly, from cast in the old bookkeeping sense of reckoning.

clue.text: See about a vessel's catch

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first word wraps the rest

parts.note: lo is an old word for look, see
taken as written
SS, steamship, is a vessel; the 's is just surface

explanation.surface: Look into what a ship has landed in its nets.
explanation.walkthrough: Catch looks like a noun for a haul of fish, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To lasso an animal is to catch it with a rope noose thrown from a distance.

clue.text: Prospering, though past one's prime

definitions.meaning: first meaning: doing well, making progress

explanation.walkthrough: The two senses look contradictory, which the surface plays on with though.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both succeeding in life and advancing in years, two separate idioms.

clue.text: Whip in the hounds, both on good and bad days

parts.note: surface padding that sets the hunting scene

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the words that follow, spanning their breaks

parts.note: the letters run across the word breaks of this phrase
surface padding completing the picture

explanation.surface: A huntsman's whip keeping the pack in order whatever the day's weather.
explanation.walkthrough: The hunting scene around the hidden letters is decoration; 'the hounds' and 'and bad days' only dress the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A thong is a narrow strip of leather, forming the lash of a whip.

clue.text: Extra paragraph out of book keeps appearing

indicators.note: something lying out of another sits on its outside, so these letters wrap round the next ones

parts.note: a postscript, PS, is a paragraph added at the end of a letter
to book a table is to reserve it

explanation.surface: An unwanted additional section keeps cropping up in a volume.
explanation.walkthrough: Book looks like a noun but is the verb; PS is a postscript added below a letter's signature.
explanation.definitionFit: To preserve something is to keep it safe and unchanged, so the verbs match.

clue.text: Bearing with an island race, none will cause contention

parts.note: south-east is a compass bearing
the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race held on the Isle of Man
zero, nothing, looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A grudge carried into an island race where nobody wins sparks a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: The TT is the famous motorbike race on the Isle of Man.
explanation.definitionFit: A set-to is a fight or heated argument, the noun for a dispute or contention.

clue.text: Found before the end of April in Switzerland

definitions.note: the place is defined by where it lies

parts.note: to found a theory on something is to base it there

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the month's last letter

explanation.surface: Something discovered just before late April in Switzerland.
explanation.walkthrough: Found looks like the past of find, but it is the verb meaning establish.
explanation.definitionFit: Basel is a city on the Rhine in northern Switzerland, so it is literally located there.

clue.text: Ring, as one arranged, for 15

indicators.note: things arranged are set out in a new order, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: the letters as written

explanation.surface: Phone up, as someone has set up, to take the place of 15.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a cross-reference: the answer stands for 15 across, THOUGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Reasoning and thought both name the mental process of thinking things through logically.

clue.text: Laughing about the Continental being so trusting

indicators.note: about here means around, so one word is placed round the other

parts.note: riant is a literary word for laughing or cheerful
el is the Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A cheerful European visitor who is naively ready to believe anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: Riant is a rare literary word; Continental signals a foreign word, here Spanish, sitting just inside the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Being reliant means depending on others, which is to put your trust in them.

clue.text: Cooked meal so hot it's really off-putting

indicators.note: something cooked is altered by the process, so the letters are changed round

parts.note: the letters as written

explanation.surface: A dish served so spicy that it puts the diner off entirely.
explanation.definitionFit: Loathsome means causing disgust or hatred, much stronger than merely unappealing.

clue.text: "Delightful task! to rear the tender -" (Thomson)

parts.note: read plainly: a line of eighteenth-century poetry about bringing up something delicate
read as a quotation to complete: the missing word from James Thomson's The Seasons

explanation.surface: A quotation from Thomson praising the joy of nurturing something young.
explanation.walkthrough: The full line from Thomson's Spring continues 'to teach the young idea how to shoot', so the gap is a word for mind or idea.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word in Thomson's line names an idea in a young mind that a teacher nurtures.

clue.text: Pearl's sleeping accommodation?

parts.note: read plainly: a woman called Pearl
read the setter's way: where a pearl lies, in a shell on the seabed

explanation.walkthrough: Pearl looks like a woman's name; the bed is a seabed full of shellfish.
explanation.definitionFit: Pearls grow inside shellfish found in a seabed colony, so that is where one rests.

clue.text: Patient handling

parts.note: read plainly: an adjective, as in calm and unhurried
read the setter's way: how a doctor deals with a person under care

explanation.walkthrough: Patient looks like an adjective meaning calm but is the noun, a person receiving medical care.
explanation.definitionFit: Medical care given to someone who is ill is called their treatment.

clue.text: Son left with some hesitation to make a false report

definitions.note: verb phrase; the answer is the verb

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son
L is the abbreviation for left
with in the sense of plus, and
er is the sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: A boy who left reluctantly, telling lies about what happened.
explanation.definitionFit: To slander someone is to spread untrue and damaging statements about them by speech.

clue.text: Once more go over touching evidence

parts.note: re means concerning, on the subject of
a trace is a sign or piece of evidence left behind

explanation.surface: Revisiting moving testimony in a case.
explanation.walkthrough: Touching suggests emotion, but means regarding, the business sense of re.
explanation.definitionFit: To retrace steps is to go back over the same route again.

clue.text: Reason for increasing warmth?

parts.note: read plainly: what causes things to heat up, like a fire or the sun
read the setter's way: the proverb that being away makes the heart grow fonder

explanation.walkthrough: Warmth is emotional, not temperature: the saying is that absence makes the heart grow fonder.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb names being away from someone as the cause of growing affection for them.

clue.text: Bill's story

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a statement of charges owed
second meaning: a narrative or report of events

explanation.walkthrough: Bill's looks like a man's possessive; it is bill is, joining two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an invoice of money owed and a description or narrative of events.

clue.text: Catechism misrepresented according to plan

indicators.note: something misrepresented is shown wrongly, so the letters are put in a wrong order

parts.note: the letters as written

explanation.surface: Church teaching twisted to fit someone's agenda.
explanation.definitionFit: Schematic describes something laid out as a diagram or scheme, following a planned outline.

clue.text: Capital cover, naturally

parts.note: read plainly: protection for a city, or insurance for money
read the setter's way: capital as the head, and the covering nature gives it

explanation.walkthrough: Capital comes from Latin caput, head; the natural cover of the head is skin bearing hair.
explanation.definitionFit: The scalp is the skin on top of the head, which grows over the skull by nature.

clue.text: Duplicated note about a resort of the USA

indicators.note: about places the doubled pieces around the next one

parts.note: mi is a note of the sol-fa scale, given twice
taken as written

explanation.surface: A repeated memo about a holiday spot in America.
explanation.walkthrough: Note suggests a written memo, but it is a musical note.
explanation.definitionFit: Miami in Florida is a famous American beach holiday destination.

clue.text: Put away about a  hundred pounds for show

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so one piece goes round the others

parts.note: to put food away is to eat it
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
L, from Latin libra, is the symbol for pounds

explanation.surface: Stashing away roughly a hundred pounds just to display it.
explanation.walkthrough: Put away looks like saving but means eating; EAT goes round C and L.
explanation.definitionFit: Eclat is brilliant display or conspicuous success, the flourish of a showy effect.

clue.text: Fasten up a climbing plant

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to nail something is to fasten it
taken as written

explanation.surface: Secure a creeper climbing a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: A liana is a woody vine that climbs trees in tropical forests.

clue.text: Soon keeping company with a . girl

parts.note: anon is an old word for soon
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who will shortly be going out with a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray dot before girl is a speck on the printed page.
explanation.definitionFit: Anona is a female first name, so it fits a clue asking for a girl's name.

clue.text: Foreshadow a stupid assessment

parts.note: taken as written
dumb is slang for stupid
a rate is a valuation or assessment

explanation.surface: A foolish evaluation hints at trouble to come.
explanation.definitionFit: To adumbrate is to give a faint indication of something in advance, the literal sense of foreshadowing.

clue.text: Coppers divided about party leader

parts.note: copper coins are pence, abbreviated P

indicators.note: the split pieces sit about, that is around, the next word

parts.note: rent means torn apart, divided
a side is a party in a dispute or contest

explanation.surface: Police split over who should head the political party.
explanation.walkthrough: Coppers suggests police, but means copper coins, pence. RENT opens to hold SIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: A president is the person at the head of a state, company or organisation.

clue.text: Plan to get a doctor back

parts.note: Dr is the title abbreviation for a doctor
aft is the back part of a ship

explanation.surface: A scheme to bring a physician home again.
explanation.walkthrough: Back looks like a return instruction, but it is simply AFT, the rear of a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A draft is a preliminary version or outline of a scheme or document.
